sources.title: InvenTree stock concurrency regression, fix, backport, release
sources.version_or_commit: Master fix `2dca27f` (PR #12718); 1.5.x backport commit `4446c95` (PR #12719); 1.5.3 release commit short `1930db0`; release dated 2026-09-08 in GitHub listing. Exact page/commit links retained, no code checkout.
sources.locator: PR #12718 body says stale pre-lock cap could cause over-consumption; commit `4446c95` diff at `src/backend/InvenTree/stock/models.py` around `take_stock` lines 3401-3422 moves cap after `lock_quantity()`, and `tests.py` adds `StockItemTakeStockConcurrencyTest` using two threads/DB connections; PR #12719 backport; release 1.5.3 bullet includes fix.
sources.access_timestamp_utc: 2026-10-09 (retrieved in 18:29–18:32 UTC research session; individual browser request timestamps not exposed)
sources.operations: Opened GitHub PR, commit diff, and releases page. Did not clone, execute upstream test, or treat reported checks as my executed checks.
sources.observations: Evidence chain: reported concurrency race → row-lock/refresh before capping quantity → cross-transaction test for phantom removal → backport and named release. Relevant to consumable depletion/write serialization, not proof of reservation correctness.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 — Range Types and Overlap Exclusion Constraints
sources.locator: Range Types §8.17.10 example exclusion on `tsrange` overlap `&&`; pair of ranges rejected and resource equality combined with `btree_gist`; CREATE TABLE exclusion syntax; SET CONSTRAINTS immediate/deferred notes.
sources.access_timestamp_utc: 2026-10-09 (retrieved in 18:29–18:32 UTC research session; individual browser request timestamps not exposed)
sources.operations: Opened official documentation only; no PostgreSQL was run.
sources.observations: DB constraint option can enforce non-overlap at commit/storage level; sample uses a time range, GiST, overlap operator, and optionally resource key + `btree_gist`. Constraint expresses only the encoded table rules; app must handle the conflict response, interval conventions, site/item identity, status/cancellation applicability, and retries.

sources.operations: Opened official docs only; no CouchDB instance or replication was run.
sources.observations: Replication keeps offline replicas useful, but concurrent doc edits can conflict and app-specific resolution is required; a deterministic document winner is not equivalent to global scheduling/unique overlapping-slot enforcement.
